title: The church brings its complaint
summary: Church members complain to Alma about persecution; Alma brings the case before King Mosiah, who consults his priests.

explicit_facts.text: Unbelievers persecute members of the church, who complain to their leaders and to Alma.
Alma lays the case before Mosiah, and Mosiah consults with his priests.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The church members can be shown presenting their complaint to Alma.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, clothing, age, and appearance of the people are not specified.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific act of persecution not described in the verse.

title: The proclamation and command
summary: Mosiah issues a proclamation against persecution. The churches are commanded to prohibit persecution, maintain equality, reject pride, esteem neighbors, and support themselves by labor; priests and teachers also work except when sick or in great want.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah sends a proclamation throughout the land that unbelievers should not persecute members of the church.
The churches are commanded to have no persecutions among them and to maintain equality among all men.
They are commanded not to let pride or haughtiness disturb their peace, to esteem neighbors as themselves, and to labor for their support.
Priests and teachers are to labor for their support, except in sickness or great want.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A proclamation being issued or read is a reasonable way to visualize the decree.
unspecified_visual_details: The proclamation's physical form, its reader, and the setting are unspecified.

narration.text: there should not any unbeliever persecute any of those who belonged to the church of God.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The commands are reported, not a separately narrated public gathering.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a public announcement scene, exact wording beyond quoted source text, or a specific labor task.

title: Peace and growth in the land
summary: The people abound in the grace of God; peace returns, the people grow numerous and spread across the land, building cities and villages. The Lord visits and prospers them, and they become large and wealthy.

explicit_facts.text: The people abound in the grace of God as they follow the described practices.
Peace returns, the people become numerous and spread north, south, east, and west, building cities and villages throughout the land.
The Lord visits and prospers them, and they become a large and wealthy people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A broad view of settlements and people spreading across the land can convey the reported growth.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance and architecture of the cities and villages, and any visible manifestation of the Lord, are unspecified.

narration.text: there began to be much peace again in the land
building large cities and villages in all quarters of the land.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord's visit is reported without a described visible appearance; do not depict a specific manifestation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not assign a specific city, building design, or visible form to the Lord.

title: Alma and the sons of Mosiah oppose the church
summary: Alma, son of Alma, and the sons of Mosiah are among the unbelievers. Alma is described as wicked and idolatrous, flattering people and leading many into his ways, harming the church. He and the sons of Mosiah secretly seek to destroy the church and lead the people astray.

explicit_facts.text: The sons of Mosiah and Alma, son of Alma, are numbered among the unbelievers; Alma is wicked and idolatrous.
Alma uses flattery and leads many to follow his iniquities, hindering the church and causing dissension.
Alma secretly goes about with the sons of Mosiah seeking to destroy the church and lead the people astray.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma and the sons of Mosiah can be shown together as they go about secretly.
unspecified_visual_details: The place, their appearance, and any particular act of persuasion are unspecified.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: Their secret opposition is summarized in narration; no specific gathering or speech is supplied.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent specific words, targets, or actions of their campaign.

title: The angel appears
summary: As Alma and the sons of Mosiah rebel, the angel of the Lord appears, descends as in a cloud, and speaks with a voice like thunder that shakes the earth. They fall to the earth in astonishment and do not understand his words.

explicit_facts.text: The angel of the Lord appears to Alma and those with him, descending as it were in a cloud.
The angel speaks with a voice like thunder, causing the earth to shake beneath them.
They fall to the earth in astonishment and do not understand his words.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The angel can be shown descending in a cloud, as explicitly described.
unspecified_visual_details: The angel's bodily appearance, clothing, and the exact landscape are unspecified.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the angel's appearance beyond the cloud-like descent.

title: The angel calls Alma to rise
summary: The angel calls Alma to arise and asks why he persecutes God's church. He says the Lord has heard the prayers of the people and Alma's father, and that he has come to convince Alma of God's power and authority.

explicit_facts.text: The angel cries out to Alma to arise and asks why he persecutes the church of God.
The angel says the Lord has heard the people's prayers and Alma's father's prayers, and that he has come to convince Alma of God's power and authority.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The angel can be shown addressing Alma and those with him at the place of the appearance.
unspecified_visual_details: The angel's appearance and whether Alma rises during this speech are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Alma, arise and stand forth, for why persecutest thou the church of God?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the angel of the Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, the Lord hath heard the prayers of his people, and also the prayers of his servant, Alma, who is thy father;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the angel of the Lord

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord as visibly present; the angel reports the Lord's words and actions.

title: The angel declares his commission
summary: The angel asks whether they can dispute God's power, points to his voice shaking the earth and his visible presence, and says he is sent from God. He tells Alma to remember the captivity of his fathers and God's deliverance, and to cease seeking to destroy the church.

explicit_facts.text: The angel asks whether they can dispute God's power, citing his voice shaking the earth and his presence before them.
The angel says he is sent from God.
The angel tells Alma to remember his fathers' captivity and God's deliverance, and to seek to destroy the church no more.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The angel can remain visibly before Alma and those with him while speaking.
unspecified_visual_details: The angel's specific appearance is not described.

spoken_dialogue.text: And can ye not also behold me before you?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the angel of the Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: Alma, go thy way, and seek to destroy the church no more,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the angel of the Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The captivity and deliverance are recalled in speech, not shown as a flashback.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the historical captivity as a present event in this scene.

title: The angel departs
summary: The angel departs after speaking. Alma and those with him fall again to the earth in astonishment, having seen the angel and heard his thunderous voice shake the earth.

explicit_facts.text: The angel's words to Alma are his last, and he departs.
Alma and those with him fall again to the earth in astonishment after seeing the angel; his voice shook the earth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The angel may be shown departing while the others are fallen to the ground.
unspecified_visual_details: The manner of departure is not stated.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the earth splitting apart; it is described as trembling as though it would.

title: Alma is carried to his father
summary: Alma becomes unable to speak or move his hands. Those with him carry him helpless until he is laid before his father.

explicit_facts.text: Alma becomes dumb and too weak to move his hands.
Those with Alma carry him helpless until he is laid before his father.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Those with Alma can be shown carrying him toward his father.
unspecified_visual_details: The route, setting, and means of carrying him are unspecified.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse describes movement to his father; no intermediate location is specified.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray a specific injury or diagnose Alma's condition.

title: Alma the Elder rejoices
summary: Alma's companions recount what happened to his father, who rejoices, recognizing God's power. He gathers a multitude to witness what the Lord has done for his son and those with him.

explicit_facts.text: Alma's companions tell his father all that happened, and his father rejoices, knowing it was God's power.
Alma's father causes a multitude to gather to witness what the Lord has done for his son and those with him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The multitude can be shown gathered near Alma and his father.
unspecified_visual_details: The place and the size or appearance of the multitude are unspecified.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The companions' account is summarized, not quoted.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the companions' report as direct dialogue.

title: The priests fast and pray
summary: He causes the priests to assemble. They fast and pray for Alma to speak and regain strength. After two days and two nights of fasting and prayer, Alma's limbs regain strength; he stands and begins to speak to them, bidding them to be of good comfort.

explicit_facts.text: An unidentified man causes the priests to assemble.
The priests begin to fast and pray to the Lord their God for Alma to speak, for his limbs to regain strength, and for the people's eyes to be opened to God's goodness and glory.
After two days and two nights of fasting and prayer, Alma's limbs regain strength; he stands and begins to speak to them, bidding them to be of good comfort.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Prayer may be conveyed through the priests' posture, without prescribing a particular gesture.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, clothing, physical appearances, number of priests, and arrangement of those present are unspecified.

narration.text: and they began to fast, and to pray to the Lord their God
the limbs of Alma received their strength, and he stood up and began to speak unto them, bidding them to be of good comfort:

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Alma's recovery follows two days and two nights of fasting and prayer; do not portray the prayer and recovery as simultaneous.
The opening of the people's eyes is a prayer request, not a narrated visible event.
The verse reports that Alma bids them to be of good comfort but does not quote his speech directly.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the man who causes the priests to assemble from these verses alone.
Do not invent Alma's spoken words or a visible supernatural effect.
Do not depict the prayer's requested opening of the people's eyes as an event that occurs.

title: Repentance and being born again
summary: A speaker says he has repented, been redeemed of the Lord, and been born of the Spirit. He recounts the Lord’s teaching that all mankind must be born again. The passage teaches that they become new creatures and otherwise cannot inherit the kingdom of God.
characters: Speaker identified as “he” in the supplied verses
The Lord, mentioned but not visibly present

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says he has repented of his sins, been redeemed of the Lord, and been born of the Spirit.
The speaker reports that the Lord told him all mankind must be born again and changed to a state of righteousness.
The passage says they become new creatures and cannot otherwise inherit the kingdom of God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The speaker may be shown speaking.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker’s appearance and surroundings are unspecified.
No visible form of spiritual rebirth is described.

spoken_dialogue.text: I have repented of my sins, and have been redeemed of the Lord; behold I am born of the Spirit.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Speaker

narration.text: all mankind, yea, men and women, all nations, kindreds, tongues and people, must be born again;
And thus they become new creatures; and unless they do this, they can in nowise inherit the kingdom of God.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Being born again and becoming new creatures are teachings, not narrated visible transformations.
The Lord’s words are reported by the speaker; no appearance of the Lord is described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not assign the speaker a name from outside the supplied verses or invent an audience.
Do not depict the Lord appearing, a visible transformation, or the kingdom of God as a visible location.

title: Alma describes his deliverance
summary: Alma says he knows the consequence of being cast off because he was nearly so. After tribulation and repentance near death, the Lord mercifully snatched him from everlasting burning; his soul is redeemed from bitterness and iniquity, and he now beholds God's light.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says he knows he might have been cast off because he was like to be cast off.
After tribulation and repentance near death, Alma says the Lord mercifully snatched him out of everlasting burning and that he is born of God.
Alma says his soul is redeemed from bitterness and iniquity and that he now beholds God's marvelous light.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma can be shown speaking to his listeners.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of everlasting burning, the abyss, and God's light is not established as a visible event.

spoken_dialogue.text: I was in the darkest abyss;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma (the Younger, rebel)

spoken_dialogue.text: but now I behold the marvelous light of God.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma (the Younger, rebel)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Abyss, burning, and light are part of Alma's figurative testimony, not narrated visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Alma in literal fire, an abyss, or a supernatural light.

title: Alma confesses his former rejection
summary: Alma says he rejected his Redeemer and denied what the fathers had spoken. He declares that the Redeemer will make himself manifest to all, and that all will bow and confess before him at judgment.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says he rejected his Redeemer and denied what had been spoken by the fathers.
Alma says the Redeemer will make himself manifest to all and that every knee will bow and every tongue confess before him at the last day.
Alma says those who live without God will acknowledge the judgment as just and will quake, tremble, and shrink beneath the all-searching eye.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma can be shown addressing the people as he continues his testimony.
unspecified_visual_details: No present visible appearance of the Redeemer or future judgment is described.

spoken_dialogue.text: every knee shall bow, and every tongue confess before him.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma (the Younger, rebel)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The last-day judgment is taught as future, not shown as a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Redeemer or a judgment scene in this moment.

title: Alma and his companions preach amid persecution
summary: From then on Alma and those who were with him at the angel's appearance travel throughout the land, teaching and publishing what they heard and saw. They endure persecution and beatings, yet console the church and exhort its members to keep God's commandments.

explicit_facts.text: Alma begins teaching and traveling through the land with those who were with him when the angel appeared, publishing what they heard and saw.
They are persecuted and beaten by unbelievers.
They console the church, confirm its faith, and exhort members to keep God's commandments.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A supported preaching or teaching setting can be used, with the persecution kept separate from the consoling church moment.
unspecified_visual_details: Specific locations, individual assailants, and the manner of the beatings are unspecified.

narration.text: they did impart much consolation to the church

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses summarize an ongoing period of travel and preaching; separate moments should not be compressed into one scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a single composition combining persecution, travel, and church consolation as simultaneous events.

title: The sons of Mosiah named
summary: The account identifies four of those who were with Alma as the sons of Mosiah: Ammon, Aaron, Omner, and Himni.

explicit_facts.text: Four of those with Alma are sons of Mosiah, named Ammon, Aaron, Omner, and Himni.

unspecified_visual_details: The verse gives names but does not describe a distinct event or setting for this identification.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is an identification in the account, not a separately described gathering.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a formal introduction or speech.

title: They seek to repair their wrongs
summary: The sons of Mosiah travel among the people under Mosiah's reign, striving to repair the injuries they did to the church, confessing their sins, and teaching those who wish to hear. They bring many to knowledge of the truth and their Redeemer, publishing peace and good tidings.

explicit_facts.text: The sons of Mosiah travel throughout Zarahemla and among those under Mosiah's reign, striving to repair injuries they had done to the church, confessing their sins, and teaching those willing to hear.
They become instruments in God's hands in bringing many to knowledge of the truth and their Redeemer.
They publish peace and good tidings and declare to the people that the Lord reigns.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The sons of Mosiah can be shown teaching people in a supported setting.
unspecified_visual_details: Specific cities, audiences, and teachings beyond the summarized account are unspecified.

narration.text: they did declare unto the people that the Lord reigneth.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses summarize their travels and work; do not combine distinct locations or occasions into one event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent particular confessions, acts of repair, or sermon content.
